author.heading: About Nassim Nicholas Taleb
author.bio: Nassim Nicholas Taleb (born 1960) is a Lebanese-American essayist, researcher and former financial trader. His Incerto books examine uncertainty, risk and the gap between formal models and lived experience; The Bed of Procrustes presents related ideas in short aphorisms rather than extended proofs.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Taleb names his book after Procrustes, the mythological host who mutilated guests to make them fit a bed. The publisher presents that story as a metaphor for forcing reality to fit rigid intellectual systems. This sharply worded analogy about academia belongs to the book’s deliberately provocative aphoristic form, rather than an empirical finding about every academic.
